## Purpose and delivery model
This is a GitHub Skills exercise repository for teaching introductory Git workflows through a small browser game. Learners copy the template, then GitHub Actions progressively prepares lessons and validates completion. The learner-facing instructions begin in `README.md`; lesson content is staged under `.github/steps/`.

## Exercise orchestration
GitHub Actions is the primary control plane. `.github/workflows/0-start-exercise.yml` initializes the copied exercise, while `.github/workflows/1-step.yml` through `.github/workflows/6-step.yml` advance or validate the six learning stages. Corresponding instructional assets live in `.github/steps/1-step.md` through `.github/steps/6-step.md`; `.github/steps/x-review.md` is the review/end-state material.

## Learner workflow boundary
The repository is intentionally designed for Git operations rather than application development alone: learners configure identity, create commits, inspect history/diffs, and work with branches. Actions respond to repository state and guide the next stage, separating automated exercise progression (`.github/workflows/`) from learner-owned project edits (`src/`).

## Sample application entry points
The editable artifact is a static client-side game:
- `src/index.html` is the browser document and application shell.
- `src/index.js` is the JavaScript entry point and runtime behavior.
- `src/style.css` provides presentation.
- `src/patterns.js` contains game pattern/content logic consumed by the client code.

There is no server-side application, API layer, database, or build system represented in the tree.

## Client-side flow
A browser loads `src/index.html`, which establishes the page structure and references styling and JavaScript. `src/index.js` drives interaction and uses pattern definitions from `src/patterns.js`; `src/style.css` controls the visual layer. This small, isolated source surface is deliberate: Git lessons can have learners add or modify features while keeping runtime complexity low.

## Development environment
The optional Codespaces/dev-container environment is defined by `.devcontainer/devcontainer.json`. Lifecycle hooks in `.devcontainer/post-create.sh` and `.devcontainer/post-start.sh` install and start the exercise-monitor integration. The monitor implementation under `.devcontainer/exercise-monitor/` observes Git activity via hooks and scripts, providing local exercise support distinct from GitHub Actions’ hosted workflow validation.

## External infrastructure
GitHub provides the template-copy onboarding flow, Actions execution, and repository collaboration context. Git itself is the central external runtime/tooling dependency, exercised through CLI and VS Code. The static sample app requires only a browser-compatible client environment; no deployed backend infrastructure is indicated.
